Article Title: Malaysia, Ethiopia for stronger defence cooperation with India as PM meets leaders
Article Text:
Discussions included defense, mining, and semiconductor cooperation.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi met his Malaysian and Ethiopian counterparts, Anwar Ibrahim and Abiy Ahmad Ali, on the sidelines of the BRICS summit on Saturday. Government sources said that meetings resulted in taking India’s relations with both countries on a new trajectory, as Malaysia and Ethiopia expressed their keenness for stronger defence cooperation with India.Joint personnel training as well as defence procurement from India was discussed, according to Indian officials. “Both countries welcomed Indian industry and Investment.Ethiopia welcomed Indian mining companies. Opportunities in the semiconductor industry were discussed with Malaysia,” said a source.According to an official readout, Modi and Ibrahim took stock of the outcomes of Modi’s visit to Malaysia in February 2026 and reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation across a range of areas, including trade and investment, defence and security, semiconductors, infrastructure, digital economy, energy, fintech, education, tourism and people-to-people ties. Ibrahim conveyed Malaysia’s concurrence to the establishment of Consulate General of India in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah.“Prime Minister Modi appreciated Malaysia’s continued support in strengthening ASEAN-India relations. The leaders exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest. They expressed their continued commitment to advancing the India-Malaysia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership,” said the Indian readout.In the meeting with the Ethiopian PM, the leaders discussed further strengthening the bilateral Strategic Partnership. They reviewed progress across key sectors, including economic cooperation, defence and security partnership, and capacity building. The meeting built on Prime Minister Modi’s historic visit to Addis Ababa in December 2025, said an Indian readout.The two leaders also exchanged perspectives on regional and international developments of mutual interest and reaffirmed their commitment to close cooperation in multilateral fora, according to Indian officials.“Prime Minister Modi expressed appreciation for Ethiopia’s participation in the 18th BRICS Summit and noted that its presence helped in reinforcing the collective voice of the Global South,” said the readout.

Article Title: PM Modi holds talks with Ethiopia, Malaysia; defence, investment on agenda
Article Text:
Sources said the talks with Ethiopia and Malaysia marked a new trajectory in India's relations with the two countries

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held separate bilateral meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in New Delhi on Saturday, with India seeking to deepen cooperation with both countries in defence, investment and emerging sectors.Sources said the talks with Ethiopia and Malaysia marked a new trajectory in India's relations with the two countries. Both expressed interest in strengthening defence cooperation with India, including joint personnel training and defence procurement, the sources said.The two countries also welcomed greater participation by Indian industry and investment. Ethiopia, in particular, expressed interest in Indian mining companies, while discussions with Malaysia covered opportunities in the semiconductor sector, according to the sources. PM Modi met Anwar on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, where Malaysia is participating as a BRICS partner country at India's invitation. The Malaysian prime minister is scheduled to deliver a national statement on "Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth" at the summit.According to Malaysia's Foreign Ministry, the country is expected to push for stronger cooperation among BRICS members and partner countries on development challenges, economic opportunities and ensuring more inclusive access to technological advances and innovation.Anwar is also scheduled to visit Kerala, with the visit aimed at strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in areas including trade and investment, the digital economy, talent and labour, education and regional connectivity.PM Modi also met Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed at Hyderabad House. Ethiopia joined BRICS as a full member in January 2024, alongside Egypt, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.The latest talks build on growing India-Ethiopia defence engagement. Earlier this month, officials from the two countries discussed ways to expand cooperation in military training, defence industry collaboration and UN peacekeeping. The discussions also covered new and emerging areas of defence cooperation.The ministry of defence had said after the meeting between Ethiopian Charge d'Affaires Nebiyu Tedla and Defence Ministry Joint Secretary Amitabh Prasad that the two sides discussed "avenues to further strengthen India-Ethiopia defence cooperation, including training, defence industry collaboration and UN Peacekeeping, with focus on new and emerging areas."
Article Summary: Sources said the talks with ethiopia and malaysia marked a new trajectory in india's relations with the two countries. Both expressed interest in strengthening defence cooperation with india, including joint personnel training and defence procurement. The two countries also welcomed greater participation by indian industry and investment.

Article Title: Xi Jinping in Delhi after 7 years: China talks 'fairness, justice', cites Brics' 'enormous potential'
Article Text:
China’s Xi heads to Brics summit with proposals to deepen Global South cooperation.

Xi expected to outline China’s priorities

China to lead Brics in 2027

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Chinese president Xi Jinping landed in New Delhi for the 18th Brics summit, where he will hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and present Beijing’s proposals for greater cooperation among Global South countries.Ahead of the meeting, China’s state-run Global Times described Brics as an increasingly important platform at a time of global uncertainty. In an editorial, the Chinese government mouthpiece said the grouping’s strength came from its commitment to openness, cooperation and fairness."The key lies in its commitment to openness and inclusiveness, its goal of win-win cooperation and its pursuit of fairness and justice. The more turbulent and transformative the world becomes, the more the unique value of Brics cooperation comes into focus. As greater Brics cooperation enters a stage of improving quality and efficiency, there is growing confidence that Brics cooperation has enormous potential and that the future of Brics countries is bright. "Xi is expected to exchange views with other leaders on the international situation, the future development of Brics and ways to deepen practical cooperation.The newspaper said Xi would also put forward China’s initiatives for expanding and improving cooperation within the grouping."Since 2013, President Xi has put forward a series of important proposals and initiatives, including the "Brics Plus" cooperation model, driving the rapid development of Brics cooperation and enabling it to deliver greater results, while playing a pivotal role at every critical juncture in the mechanism's development."The editorial also highlighted China’s support for the New Development Bank, the expansion of Brics and cooperation in areas such as peace, innovation, green development and people-to-people exchanges."From advocating the Brics Spirit of "openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation" to proposing the concept of the "Brics Plus" cooperation model; from championing the establishment of the New Development Bank in Shanghai to supporting the historic expansion of Brics and proposing to build a Brics committed to peace, innovation, green development, justice and closer people-to-people exchanges, China has actively worked to strengthen and expand Brics cooperation, continuously improved the mechanism in line with changing times and steadily enhanced its global influence, earning broad recognition from all sides," the editorial adds.China will take over the rotating Brics presidency in 2027. The Global Times said Beijing would use the term to strengthen unity through multilateralism and align development strategies among member countries.It said China would also promote its Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative. The newspaper identified the digital economy, green development, artificial intelligence, poverty reduction and agriculture as areas where China would seek concrete outcomes.The editorial concluded, "A 'Greater Brics' that is more united, efficient, pragmatic and committed to shouldering its responsibilities will surely open up new space for the common development of the Global South and inject greater certainty and positive energy into a world beset by turbulence and change."India is hosting the 18th Brics summit under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”. The agenda focuses on development, sustainability, innovation and strengthening the grouping as a constructive forum for the Global South.
Article Summary: China’s xi heads to brics summit with proposals to deepen global south cooperation. Xi expected to outline china's priorities for the meeting. China will take over the rotating brics presidency in 2027. The agenda focuses on development, sustainability, innovation and strengthening the grouping.

Article Title: China Southern to resume Guangzhou-Delhi flights after 6 years ahead of Xi's Brics visit
Article Text:
Air connectivity between India and China has gradually improved in recent months.

Direct air links between India and China return

Xi leaves for Brics summit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

China Southern Airlines will restart regular passenger flights between Guangzhou and New Delhi from September 21, the Global Times reported on Saturday.The announcement came ahead of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s visit to India for the Brics summit. The airline said the resumption would take its total operations across eight round-trip routes in South Asia to more than 100 flights a week. The Guangzhou-New Delhi service had been suspended for six years.Air connectivity between India and China has gradually improved in recent months.Air China resumed its Beijing-Delhi service in April, while China Eastern Airlines restarted direct flights between Kunming and Kolkata on April 18.Indian carrier IndiGo also launched a daily non-stop service between Kolkata and Shanghai on March 30. The airline had earlier restored flights from Kolkata to Guangzhou and later began operating from Delhi to the Chinese city.The resumption of direct flights followed confirmation from India’s ministry of external affairs. Air links between the two countries had been suspended during the Covid-19 pandemic and amid tensions following the Doklam and Galwan standoffs.Xi left Beijing on Saturday for the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi at Modi’s invitation, China’s state news agency Xinhua reported.The Chinese president is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later in the day.Xi’s delegation includes Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China and director of its General Office, and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.According to Xinhua, Xi is expected to advance proposals on cooperation among Global South countries, building on his remarks at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.Brics has become a major platform for emerging economies to coordinate on trade, finance, technology, development and global governance. The grouping also seeks to promote greater cooperation among countries of the Global South.

The resumption would take its total operations across eight round-trip routes in south asia to more than 100 flights a week. Air links between the countries had been suspended during the covid-19 pandemic and amid tensions following the doklam and galwan standoffs.

Article Title: PM gifts Putin Russian version of Tamil text 'Thirukkural'
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A Russian translation of 'Thirukkural', the influential Tamil work whose wisdom PM Narendra Modi has often drawn on in his speeches, was his gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin Friday as they met ahead of the Brics summit.The ancient book carries 1,330 short couplets offering moral guidance on principally three pursuits - virtue, govt and society, and love. Besides Modi, parliamentarians, especially those from Tamil Nadu, often quote from it. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has drawn from it during her budget speeches and so has P Chidambaram when he was in office.While the book offers wisdom on the strategy for war when needed, it also emphasises the virtue of peace - a principle Modi has often advocated by stressing the need to avoid conflicts. In their past meetings, he has nudged Putin to end the Ukraine conflict, which is now in its fifth year."Presented President Putin with a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, which carries the eternal wisdom of the great Thiruvalluvar across languages and borders," Modi said.

Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti-West.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.
Article Summary: Shashi tharoor says govt must keep brics non-west and not let it appear anti-west. He also said that pm modi's scheduled meeting with chinese president xi jinping and the meeting with russian president vladimir putin "are going to grab world headlines" the summit will bring together leaders of brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.

Article Title: Russia & Iran hit out at US 'aggression', pose a challenge for summit host India

New Delhi: Russia and Iran Friday hit out at US and other Western powers for imposing sanctions and "acts of aggression", and called upon Brics to work on strategies that make the group more resilient to deal with challenges and pressures, in what underlined the challenge India faces in seeking to stop the meeting from turning into an anti-West platform."Iran has faced extensive sanctions over the past years. However, in recent months, these pressures have entered a far more dangerous phase as a result of the military act of aggression of US and the Israelis against Iran. This... in addition to material losses, once again revealed an important reality: economic security cannot be separated from national and regional security," Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said at Brics Business Forum."Whenever the trade energy infrastructure or the financial system of a country comes under political or military pressure, its effects extend beyond the country's borders and can affect regional or even global stability," he said.Russian President Vladimir Putin hit out at the "old leaders" resorting to "every conceivable means to reclaim their erstwhile dominance".He said, "They go so far as to employ instruments of direct physical force, including the destruction of industrial and logistical infrastructure...Efforts are under way to block international transport corridors, to seize sea-going vessels, while illegal restrictions are imposed, accompanied by threats of so-called secondary sanctions, on those who refuse to act in the interests of others and instead seek to defend their own national interests. "The speeches offered a glimpse into the task awaiting India, which will be called upon to reconcile the hostility with its own policy of flexible multi-alignment. India is aware that the Trump administration will be keeping a close watch on the Brics deliberations because of Russia and Iran's anger over sanctions and China's interest in pushing for moves such as de-dollarisation and a cross-border payment system that can rival West-controlled SWIFT. US President Donald Trump has made no bones of his opposition to Brics.Putin sought investment platforms to fund projects in trade, infrastructure and technology. "We are ready to contribute to the world's energy and food security with our partners, and to jointly shape reliable global routes, such as Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor and North-South International Corridor," he said.Pezeshkian said, "Food and energy security are two fundamental pillars of economic security, and Iran, with its vast energy reserves and outstanding geographical position, is prepared to play the role of a strategic partner in Brics food, energy and transport supply chains."He batted for expanding tr-ade in local currency, building a reinsurance pool with a $10 billion initial corpus, and fina-ncing infrastructure through New Development Bank. Putin, too, backed NDB and sought leveraging it to create a new investment platform.
Article Summary: Russia and iran friday hit out at us and other western powers for imposing sanctions. They called upon brics to work on strategies that make the group more resilient. The speeches offered a glimpse into the task awaiting india, which will be called upon to reconcile the hostility with its own policy of flexible multi-alignment.

Article Title: Trump’s ‘deepest, darkest China’ gets a Brics sequel with Iran's cameo as India walks tightrope
Article Text:
PM Modi, Pezeshkian & Putin at Brics Summit 2026 (left); PM Modi, Xi and Putin at SCO summit in 2025 (right)

Trump pressure on Brics

India walks a tight rope

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What could be a fresh diplomatic headache for Donald Trump? A picture of Prime Minister Narendra Modi holding hands with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with Russian President Vladimir Putin standing alongside them at the Brics Summit , has brought together three countries whose ties with Washington range from strategic competition to open confrontation.The image also echoes a remark Trump made last year after PM Modi, Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping were pictured together at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. “Looks like we’ve lost India and Russia to deepest, darkest, China. May they have a long and prosperous future together!” Trump had said.This time, Iran, one of Washington’s most adversarial rivals, has joined the picture, adding another layer to the geopolitical message from a grouping that Trump has repeatedly viewed with suspicion. The US president has not yet commented on the Brics summit.US President Donald Trump has repeatedly warned Brics against challenging the dominance of the US dollar, putting the grouping’s push for greater use of local currencies at the centre of tensions with Washington. In November 2024, Trump threatened 100% tariffs on Brics countries if they backed another currency to replace the dollar.“We require a commitment from these Countries that they will neither create a new Brics Currency, nor back any other currency to replace the mighty US Dollar or, they will face 100% Tariffs, and should expect to say goodbye to selling into the wonderful US economy,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social.Trump has also dismissed the prospect of Brics replacing the dollar in global trade, saying there was “no chance” of that happening and warning that countries attempting to do so should “wave goodbye to America”.The issue remains central to Brics’ economic agenda, although the grouping has increasingly focused on making trade and payments in national currencies easier rather than creating a common currency. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, speaking at the Brics Business Forum, called for greater use of national currencies among members, along with mechanisms to manage currency risks and facilitate reciprocal settlements.“One of the most important steps is to expand the use of national currencies in trade among the members. This step must be accompanied by the establishment of the necessary instruments for managing currency risks and reciprocal settlements,” Pezeshkian said.He also argued that the existing financial system was vulnerable because of its concentration around a limited number of currencies and called for the New Development Bank to play a bigger role in financing infrastructure and energy projects through local currencies and other mechanisms.Putin, meanwhile, did not directly mention replacing the dollar at this year’s forum. Instead, he described a broader shift in the global economic order, with emerging economies becoming increasingly important.“Right now, the world is undergoing structural, deep, profound shifts. It is explained by the fact that the so-called old leaders which used to be the vanguard of economic growth in the second half of the 20th century, are being replaced by new engines of growth. When I say old, this is just a formality - all of us understand what we are talking about,” he said.For Washington, the concern is not simply whether Brics creates a new currency, but whether a larger share of global trade and financial transactions gradually moves away from the dollar.For India, the Brics summit comes at a sensitive point in its economic relationship with the US. The India-US trade deal is “more or less” finalised, with the two sides working on a framework for preferential market access before signing it at an appropriate time. A few issues remain under discussion.The talks come as Trump continues to step up pressure on India over its purchase of Russian oil. In 2025, he had warned of further tariff action and later imposed 50% tariffs on Indian goods, adding to the economic stakes for New Delhi as it seeks to deepen trade with the US.India is meanwhile pursuing multiple trade agreements to widen market access. It has signed nine trade agreements over the past five years covering economies with a combined GDP of $60 trillion, while talks with Chile are at an advanced stage and New Zealand has been targeted for an early rollout.The balancing act is also reflected in India’s broader trade priorities. Its total exports reached $863 billion in 2025-26, including $421 billion in services, with the government seeking to diversify services exports beyond IT and professional services and expand areas such as fintech and digital services.The conflict involving Iran and the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz have added another layer to the equation. The waterway is a crucial route for global oil shipments, making stability in the Gulf directly relevant to India’s energy security, trade and the safety of Indian seafarers.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump has repeatedly warned brics against challenging the dominance of the us dollar. The grouping’s push for greater use of local currencies is at the centre of tensions with washington. In november 2024, trump threatened 100% tariffs on brics countries if they backed another currency to replace the dollar.

Article Title: Guarding Xi: Inside heightened security deployment
Article Text:
This will be Xi Jinping's first India visit since 2019

NEW DELHI: From establishing temporary no-fly zones over his hotel to conducting checks for potential so-called CBRN (Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear) threats, President Xi Jinping’s security during his 24-hour visit to India is expected to reach an unprecedented scale.The security measures are attributed mainly to the perceived threat from a lone-wolf attack or even demonstrations by Tibetan activists. Beijing has warned specifically about the possible use of drones, banners, loudspeakers and balloons as tools for anti-China propaganda and sought effective measures to keep out low-altitude, small-size aerial objects and other UAVs.Xi will land in Delhi around noon on Saturday, accompanied by a 67-member govt entourage comprising senior political figures, diplomats, security officials and medical staff.“All security concerns and issues raised by foreign govts are being addressed as per MEA (ministry of external affairs) protocol in coordination with Delhi Police and other agencies,” said an official source requesting anonymity.Ten days before the visit, China flew in a planeload of cargo items including Xi’s car, Hongqi (red flag) state limousine, another backup car and communication equipment. India allows foreign delegations to carry their own communication equipment, subject to approval by department of telecommunications.Satellite communication equipment is not allowed.In the case of guns and ammunitions, while pistols are allowed, items like sub machine guns and anti-drone equipment cannot be imported and must be left with customs at the airport on arrival.Apart from attending a Brics summit session on Saturday, Xi will have a bilateral meeting with PM Narendra Modi and join him later for a state dinner. Indian authorities have been requested by the Chinese to allow Xi’s staff to access the kitchen, apparently to sample some of the dishes on the menu and ensure they conform to the president’s dietary preferences. Like with the millet-heavy G20 menu, food on this occasion too is likely to be vegetarian.Apart from deployment of counter-terrosism forces and anti-explosion devices, the president’s hotel will also undergo comprehensive anti-nuclear, anti-radiation and anti-biochemical security checks ahead of his arrival. Security measures also include an inspection of the underground pipeline networks. Xi will be in India for 24 hours and will depart for the airport from Bharat Mandapam around 11 am on Sunday.

Beijing has warned specifically about the possible use of drones, banners, loudspeakers and balloons as tools for anti-china propaganda. China flew in a planeload of cargo items including xi’s car, hongqi (red flag) state limousine.

Article Title: Shashi Tharoor answers Chidambaram’s questions on Brics benefits for India; BJP takes digs
Article Text:
It's Congress vs Congress again, this time over Brics Summit that is being held in Delhi.

Tharoor joins debate

Tharoor vs Congress

NEW DELHI: Shashi Tharoor not being in sync with his Congress colleagues is no longer news. Especially, if the issue in question pertains to the global stage. So, when senior Congress leader Chidambaram questioned the benefits of Brics for India, Tharoor had an answer. As expected, the answer triggered another round of Tharoor vs Congress debate that overshadowed the BJP broadside against Chidambaram.On Wednesday, Chidambaram questioned the tangible benefits India has gained from recent Brics summits, and said he had not seen any significant outcomes from the last two or three meetings.“I don't know how many presidents and how many prime ministers are coming. I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results,” Chidambaram stated. “In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of QUAD. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Chidambaram’s remarks opened the floodgates for counter-attacks from the ruling party. The BJP leaders launched a broadside against Chidambaram and the Congress. What followed was a barrage of attacks ranging from "Dimagi Naxal", "Naraz Fufas in pain", "FOMO", "indigestion", "bitten by bug" to questions on what Congress had gained in diplomacy since Independence"Is diplomacy to be seen as a transaction like the Congress Party is projecting? What have I done for you? What will you do for me? Kind of an approach.What is the so-called tangible result?" BJP leader Nalin Kohli wondered.Kohli then questioned the Congress party's own diplomatic record from Independence until 2014. "If we talk of tangible results, we can question what the Congress Party's entire approach from 1947 right up to 2014 was on diplomacy, including Sharm El Sheikh and projecting Pakistan as literally a victim of terror when it is the perpetrator of terror," he stated.Tharoor then joined the debate and said India holding Brics was a matter of prestige. "Having a dozen heads of state and government, not only members of Brics but also some observers coming at presidential and prime ministerial level, is a matter of great prestige for us. It shows a certain diplomatic convening power, which has value in and of itself on the global stage," Tharoor said.The Congress MP maintained that the Brics Summit is providing an important platform for the Global South."This grouping, the 11 Brics countries, represents a majority of the world's population and 41 per cent of global GDP. It's not a small matter; it's something that has to be taken very seriously by the rest of the world. Secondly, of course, having a dozen heads of state and government, not only members of BRICS but also some observers coming at the presidential and prime ministerial level, this is a matter of great prestige for us," the Congress MP from Thiruvananthapuram said.Latching onto Tharoor’s remarks, Nalin Kohli said: “One has noted Dr Shashi Tharoor's statement, and anyone who understands diplomacy would see great value in the BRICS summit.”BJP leader Pradeep Bhandari also used Tharoor’s remarks to take digs at the Congress and allege that some party leaders were opposing Brics on the instructions of Rahul Gandhi “Congress exposes Congress! Congress MP Shashi Tharoor says-" BRICS happening in India is a matter of huge prestige for Bharat." Congress MP exposes "Naraz Fufa" of Congress who were opposing BRICS on instructions of Rahul Gandhi!” Pradeep Bhandari said in a post on X.Tharoor has had frosty ties with the Congress over his “independent views” on a range of issues. In the last two years, Tharoor has often made the Congress duck for cover as the BJP has cited his views to school the grand-old-party. The Thiruvananthapuram MP has made several remarks over a wide range of issues - from lessons in nationalism to global diplomacy to the Emergency to Covid-19 vaccine distribution abroad - that have brought more cheers to the BJP than his own party, the Congress.It all started with Tharoor's surprise "out-of-turn" praise for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s US trip after Donald Trump took oath as president for a second term.Tharoor then acknowledged key achievements from PM Modi’s visit, particularly on trade negotiations and defence cooperation. He welcomed the trade deal discussions and expressed optimism over India’s diplomatic engagements.The Congress immediately issued a clarification, which said that individual opinions do not reflect the party’s official stance. But Tharoor defended his remarks and said: “When someone in the government does the right thing, it should be recognised, irrespective of who's in power. For 16 years, I have been in politics. My attitude has been that when somebody in the government, whether it’s our government or some other party’s government, does the right thing or does something well, one should acknowledge and praise it, and when they do something badly, one should criticise it. If I were to praise all the time, no one would take me seriously. If I were to criticise all the time, no one would take me seriously either… There’s got to be some give and take in democracy.”After the Pahalgam terror attack and Centre's Operation Sindoor, Tharoor made several remarks that were at variance with the official stand taken by the Congress.Tharoor was picked up to lead a multi-party parliamentary delegation to represent India globally following Operation Sindoor. Later, writing for The Hindu, Tharoor praised Modi’s "energy, dynamism, and willingness to engage" as a major asset for India on the global stage. He described Modi’s multi-alignment strategy as a key pillar in projecting India's voice globally.At one stage, Tharoor said Modi’s foreign policy was remarkable as the Prime Minister was maintaining excellent relations with Russia while simultaneously pursuing strategic relations with the USA. Modi has raised Bharat as a powerful and independent force and has put forward a policy of “multi-alignment”.In May last year, during the inauguration of the Vizhinjam International Seaport in Thiruvananthapuram, Prime Minister Modi acknowledged the presence of Tharoor on stage and remarked that it would give "sleepless nights" to many in the opposition INDIA bloc.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi held a meeting with Tharoor in January this year ahead of assembly elections in Kerala and tried to sort out the differences and project a unified picture.Tharoor has all along defended his remarks and has claimed that his stand on several international issues was "pro-India, and not pro-BJP," stressing that national interest transcends party lines.Clearly, for Shashi Tharoor, his remarks on Brics are par for the course. It is the Congress that has to decide - how to handle the independent views of its MP from Thiruvananthapuram.
Article Summary: It's congress vs congress again, this time over brics summit that is being held in delhi. Tharoor joins debate and says india holding brics was a matter of prestige. Bjp leaders launched a broadside against chidambaram and the congress.

Article Title: 40% of global GDP is here: PM Modi
Article Text:
PM Modi will fellow Brics leaders in New Delhi

PM Modi

's 'Intra-Brics trade' call seen as aimed at US and China

NEW DELHI: Noting that the Brics grouping now represents 50% of the global population, 40% of GDP, and 25% of trade, PM Narendra Modi said Friday that their collective economic might has grown at nearly double the global pace since the bloc was formed in 2006, and called upon member countries to reduce barriers to trade and increase opportunities for businesses.In his address at the Brics Business Forum, PM also underlined the need to keep trade flowing. "Global trade can move forward only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes are open, and seafarers are safe. And, therefore, Bharat is a firm supporter of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers," Modi said, his remark coming against the backdrop of disruption of traffic through Strait of Hormuz and the growing threat through Bab al-Mandab Strait, another crucial artery for India.His pitch for deeper engagement significantly contrasted the themes of 2 other key members: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.Putin, like PM, also invoked the growing economic heft of Brics members. However, he and Pezeshkian, with their countries reeling from sanctions, were resentful of the West's continuing sway."The world is changing... Over the past 5 years, as it has been said today - I think it was our Indonesian colleague who said it, the Brics countries accounted for over 40% of global GDP, while the contribution of Group of Seven, the so-called leading economies, although I don't understand why they are called 'leading', was just 29%," Putin said.At a time when trade barriers are increasing, India is building economic bridges, PM Narendra Modi said, adding, “Our approach in Brics is also the same: to reduce barriers and increase opportunities for businesses.”He has been averse to Brics being turned into an anti-West bloc and has resisted the push from China, Russia and Iran for de-dollarisation. Also, his call for greater intra-Brics commerce can be seen as aimed at both US President Trump’s strong arm tariff tactics as well as a reminder of New Delhi’s contention to China that it needed to let in more Indian goods and should not weaponise supplies of equipment and raw materials needed by Indian manufacturers.“In these years, the combined GDP of Brics countries has grown by about 4.5 times while the global GDP has grown by around 2.5 times. Brics’s economic strength has grown at nearly double the pace of the world,” Modi said, pointing to the bloc comprising emerging markets and developing economies.He called upon the Brics Business Council to identify the top 10 trade barriers to be removed, while charting the growth trajectory of the Indian economy in the last 12 years since his govt took office with its focus on innovation and resilience.“Can we support 100 Brics startups every year to scale in other Brics markets? Can we develop 1,000 new partnerships among our businesses? On all these benchmarks, we have to review our progress every year. Let us turn the ambition of Brics into action and its collective strength into global solutions. Let Brics move forward and take the world forward as well.”Lauding Brics nations for becoming key centres for global innovation and solutions — from grassroots to frontier tech — he said the bloc’s growing scale, speed, and optimism are clearly visible.With the theme of India’s Brics presidency being “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Co-operation and Sustainability”, he said India has made this foundation of its economic and trade policy.India has made supply chains from energy to technology more diversified and reliable, he said, adding that it is offering confidence in growth and stability even amid global uncertainties.“We are rapidly expanding roads, railways, ports, and airports. Along with this, we are building new capabilities in strategic sectors such as ship-building, semiconductor, quantum, critical minerals, and bio-tech,” he said.Turning to his govt’s call to the global business for “Make in India, Innovate with India, Scale for the World”, he said the country has more than two lakh start-ups, and over 120 unicorns, which are transforming education and healthcare through AI, crossing new frontiers in defence and space, and working on green hydrogen and batteries as well.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi said brics' economic might has grown at nearly double the global pace since the bloc was formed in 2006. He called upon member countries to reduce barriers to trade and increase opportunities for businesses. His pitch for deeper engagement significantly contrasted the themes of 2 other key members: russian president vladimir putin and iranian president masoud pezeshkian.

NEW DELHI: Ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s arrival in New Delhi for the ongoing Brics Summit, Chinese Ambassador to India Xu Feihong said on Friday that China will work with India to ensure the two countries remain “friends enjoying good-neighbourliness and partners helping each other succeed. ”"China and India are arranging a bilateral meeting between President Xi and Prime Minister Modi. Article Title: PM doubles down on friendship with Iran, seeks win-win strategy; hope mounts for BRICS declaration

PM Modi-Pezeshkian meeting

NEW DELHI: After calling for expanding and diversifying India’s trade basket with Iran, PM Narendra Modi doubled down on ties with Tehran as he discussed with President Masoud Pezeshkian India-Iran “friendship” and agreed the two countries should move forward with a “long-term and win-win strategy”.The leaders met for the second time in 2 weeks, walking hand-in-hand at the BRICS Business Forum meeting alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin. Modi reiterated that all issues related to the West Asia conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.“From Bishkek to Delhi, the productive discussions continue. Happy to have met Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian, the President of Iran. This visit is more special because it is his first visit to India,” said Modi in a post on X, adding India remains steadfast in its commitment to the pursuit of enduring peace.Pezeshkian is the first Iranian president to visit India in 8 years. India is hoping both Iran and the UAE will show more flexibility in addressing the West Asia situation at the BRICS summit, allowing a joint BRICS declaration, unlike what happened earlier in the foreign ministers’ meeting. Official sources said they were positive about a constructive outcome in the ongoing talks for a unified declaration, with support forthcoming from all member-states.‎In their recent meeting in Bishkek, Modi had called for expanding the trade basket with Iran despite the US sanctions against Tehran. India rejects unilateral sanctions, complying only with UN-backed action. Interestingly, Pezeshkian was received at the airport by India’s Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Shantanu Thakur who oversees cooperation with Iran on the strategic Chabahar port project. In the meeting, Pezeshkian called for maintaining bilateral strategic agreements.According to an Indian readout, the PM underscored the need for continued efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in the region, safeguarding freedom of navigation and commerce, and the safety and well-being of seafarers.Modi also thanked Iran for its regular, high-level participation in BRICS-related meetings despite the “challenging circumstances”.“He noted the potential for BRICS in building the spirit of resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability among countries in the Global South. He also thanked President Pezeshkian for his participation in the Leaders’ Session of the BRICS Business Forum,” said the Indian readout, adding that the PM appreciated the continued cooperation between the two sides on issues of mutual interest in multilateral organizations, including BRICS.Before the bilateral meeting, Pezeshkian said at the business forum meeting that geopolitical uncertainty, disruptions to supply chains and the growing use of economic instruments to exert political pressure had made the environment for economic activity increasingly complex.Pezeshkian called for expanding the use of national currencies in trade among member-states, saying this step must be accompanied by the creation of necessary mechanisms for managing currency risks and reciprocal settlement because the current financial system is vulnerable to political shocks.The president proposed that BRICS establish a reinsurance company with initial capital of $ 10 billion to cover the risks of major infrastructure and energy projects and increase the confidence of the private sector.

Article Title: Modi reiterates peace message before Putin as efforts to end war gain momentum
Article Text:
PM Modi and Vladimir Putin at Brics Summit in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: Amid renewed efforts to resolve the Ukraine crisis, PM Narendra Modi reiterated before President Vladimir Putin that dialogue and diplomacy was the way forward in resolving conflicts and India stood ready to assist in peace efforts. The leaders met on the margins of the BRICS summit – their third encounter in the past 9 months – and discussed ways to enhance cooperation in a range of areas including trade, defence, energy, mobility, critical minerals, fertilisers and people-to-people contacts.PM Modi and Putin had last met on August 31 in Bishkek on the sidelines of the SCO summit, where Modi stressed it was time to bring the “endless” Russia-Ukraine war to an end. In between the 2 leaders’ meetings, external affairs minister S Jaishankar travelled to Kyiv and discussed “approaches” to end the ongoing conflict with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.Modi’s repeated counsel for peace to Putin is significant as India explores ideas and suggestions that could be developed for cessation of the conflict. For good measure, PM gifted to Putin a Russian translation of Tamil literary masterpiece Thirukkural that inspired Mahatma Gandhi and Leo Tolstoy’s philosophy of non-violence.Modi said the classic carried the eternal wisdom of the great Thiruvalluvar across languages and borders.The meeting on Friday also saw the PM raising the issue of the safety of Indian seafarers. Modi, who accepted Putin’s invitation to visit Russia this year for the annual leaders’ summit, said in a post on X that he was delighted to meet Putin in Delhi, less than two weeks after their meeting in Bishkek.“During today’s meeting we talked about: Closer trade ties, including implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030. Cooperation in areas like infrastructure, energy, technology, defence, culture and more. India’s efforts during our BRICS Presidency aimed at furthering the welfare of our planet,” said the PM, sharing details about the meeting.According to an Indian readout, like in Bishkek, they shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers. The same formulation was used for the Bishkek meeting.“The two leaders agreed to remain engaged in an effort to strengthen further the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two countries, which continues to register significant growth and has shown resilience in the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties,” said the Indian readout.The 2 sides also discussed the strategic importance of critical minerals for emerging technologies and advanced manufacturing, reiterating their interest – as underlined by the leaders after the last annual summit in December 2025 - in joint exploration, processing and recycling technologies of critical minerals and rare earths.India and Russia are also looking to broaden cooperation in nuclear energy, including fuel cycle, life cycle support for operating Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant. Continued supply of fertilisers is an immediate priority for India and Putin said last month, in a meeting with Jaishankar, that Russia will increase export to meet the demands of Indian farmers.Modi and Putin also welcomed Russia’s International Industrial Exhibition INNOPROM India, which was held for the first time in India from September 9 to 11, and underscored its importance in further expanding trade and industrial ties. The two leaders also visited the INNOPROM India exhibition and interacted with the participants, said the Indian statement.
Article Summary: The leaders met on the margins of the brics summit – their third encounter in the past 9 months. They discussed ways to enhance cooperation in a range of areas including trade, defence, energy, mobility, critical minerals, fertilisers and people-to-people contacts. Modi gifted to putin a russian translation of tamil literary masterpiece thirukkural.
